title: Scrotal ultrasound
what: The doctor uses ultrasound to look at the testicles and the tissue around them. It is safe, uses no radiation, and does not hurt.
why: For pain, swelling, or a lump in the scrotum, after an injury, or for problems getting pregnant with a partner.
tell_doctor: When your symptoms started and what bothers you
If you have had injuries or surgery in the groin or scrotum
If you feel a testicle is not in its usual place

prepare.title: Preparation
prepare.text: No special preparation is needed. You can eat and drink as usual.

prepare.title: Hygiene
prepare.text: Take a shower before the scan. You will feel more at ease.

bring: Past ultrasound reports, if you have them
A tissue or towel to wipe off the gel
steps: You undress below the waist and lie on your back
The penis is covered with a tissue
The doctor puts on cool gel
The probe is gently moved over the scrotum
Sometimes you are asked to strain or stand up. This shows the veins
feel: The probe presses only lightly. If the area is sore, it may be unpleasant. Tell the doctor
after: The gel is wiped off, and you can go back to your day right away
You usually get the report right away
The doctor who referred you will tell you what to do next
red_flags: Sudden severe pain in a testicle: do not wait for a planned scan. Call emergency services right away
A testicle suddenly swells or turns red, or you feel sick or vomit

faq.a: No. The probe just touches the skin. It can feel unpleasant only if the testicle is already sore.

faq.q: Why can't I wait with sudden pain in a testicle?
faq.a: The testicle may twist and lose its blood supply. It can only be saved in the first few hours. Call emergency services right away.
